chapter: Learning from Fletcher's circle in New York
title: Sorting out when he graduated from Wilberforce
summary: The interviewer tries to pin down Horace's graduation date; he needed summer school to finish his senior year and recalls the walk with his father that summer. The date stays unsettled.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Now, most of this is going on during the Summers, between your years at --
(inaudible)
Wilberforce. And then, do you recall the year that you graduated or finished?
It was in the thirties, I think, the late thirties. I had some of that stuff, (inaudible)
I have just one report here which states that it -- your graduation has not been ascertained, and I was just wondering if you recall that.

In fact, you can clear that up. I -- my fourth year, which was my senior year, we were doing so well till I had to go back. This is the only year -- I'm glad you mentioned that -- that I didn't get back into New York. I had to go to summer school to finish. And this was in the late thirties, I'm sure. Now, I'm looking at something here --
Did you -- well -- did you go into school right after high school -- I mean did you go on to Atlanta and then to Wilberforce and then --
Yes. Yes.
So actually, if you were born in 1904 -- is that correct? -- Okay --
Say that quietly. Quietly.
All right. Listen, my father, who's -- he was born earlier than that. That would have put you in school around like -- let's see -- 20 -- 1925 when you would of -- 1926 for a normal graduation.
Then that would have been the early Thirties, (inaudible) wouldn't it?
Well, if you were say 21 or 22 when you graduated, would you have been that age? It's not important but I was just wondering.
(Unintelligible) somewhere here now. We're off I'm looking at something here. I think it's the early thirties. We're gonna have to check on that.
Well, yeah. Maybe you have a diploma or something, even someplace.
That's something I can look up. That'll settle it.
Yeah. Let's not worry about that now. What I was getting at was just sort of timing of all of this.
Right.
After you -- let's see, you went to summer school then -- what, between your junior and senior year, or after your senior year -- what would have been your senior year.
I had to complete my senior year during the summer. I missed an entire semester. I didn't have enough credits, you know, to go through.
Yeah. I did that.
I had to -- I remember that so well. This was when my father came up, you know, that summer time. It was in Real summer, cause it was hot, we took this walk.
